correctness.rationale: For H=lambda_perp I+Delta uu^T the Ritz optimum is squared norm of u projected onto span(v,x), so the exact spectral-gap factor is W=1-(p dot x)^2. A uniform tangent x in dimension d-1 has squared fixed-direction overlap Beta(1/2,(d-2)/2); thus each W is Beta(a_d,1/2), a_d=(d-2)/2, and conditional distribution independent of past proves the factors iid. The exact gamma-ratio formula for E[W^q] holds for q>-a_d, and at k_d=floor(cd) its scaled log moment generating function converges for theta<1/2 to -c/2 log(1-2theta). The derivative range (0,infinity), tilted variance O(1/d), and exponential tightness prove full speed-d LDP with I_c(s)=(s-c-c log(s/c))/2 on s>0 and +infinity for s<=0, plus the two one-sided exponent statements. Under all finite d>=3 the gap stays positive almost surely. The package verify.py was read and checks independent Ritz eigensolutions; no finite tests are used as the LDP proof.

value.rationale: The probability of obtaining a specified multiplicative Rayleigh-error reduction after a budget proportional to dimension is a natural algorithm-reliability question. The exact two-sided rare-event exponent distinguishes expected contraction from high-probability performance and supplies precise success/failure thresholds inaccessible from expectation alone. The new joint asymptotic is a substantive motivated classification even though its Beta and Gamma ingredients are classical.
